title: QUIZ - 22
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Use a map scale ratio to convert a map distance into a real-world distance
questions.question: On a map with a scale of 1:200, a distance of 10 cm represents how many cm in real life?
questions.explanation: A scale of \(1:200\) means that 1 map cm represents 200 real cm. Therefore, \(10\text{ cm}\times\frac{200\text{ cm}}{1\text{ cm}}=2000\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Multiply the map distance by the scale factor to get the real-world distance.

questions.learningObjective: Use a scale ratio to find a scaled-down model's dimensions from a real measurement
questions.question: A scale model uses a ratio of 1:50. If the real object is 750 cm long, how long is the model?
questions.explanation: A 1:50 scale means the real object is 50 times as long as the model, so the model length is \(750 \div 50 = 15\) cm.
questions.hint: Divide the real-world length by the scale factor to find the model's length.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the squared relationship between linear scale factor and area
questions.question: A scale model uses a linear scale of 1:4. If the model's square base has an area of 64 square units, what is the area of the actual base?
questions.explanation: When lengths scale by a factor of \(4\), areas scale by the square of that factor, \(4^2=16\). Therefore, the actual area is \(64\text{ square units}\times 16=1024\text{ square units}\).
questions.hint: Area scales by the square of the linear scale factor, not the same factor as length.
